source_uses.fact: EIA under the 2017 Regulations applies to projects likely to have significant environmental effects and requires project-specific screening/scoping and assessment
SEA/SA are plan-making tools and are distinct from project-level Environmental Impact Assessment
HRA screening asks whether likely significant effects on a habitats site can be excluded; if not, appropriate assessment is required
Competent authorities must follow HRA stages and a precautionary approach for protected European sites
PINS HRA advice was updated 14 July 2026 and distinguishes screening, appropriate assessment and derogations
Planning authorities must provide enough environmental information for statutory bodies to comment; EIA and HRA cases have specific consultation evidence needs
The 2026 Draft London Plan IIA includes SA/SEA, Health, Community Safety and Equalities assessment, with HRA reported separately
MD3515 notes the IIA and HRA prepared for the Draft London Plan and opened statutory consultation on 16 July 2026
Current consultation resources provide the supporting evidence and assessments for review; they remain draft-plan evidence
Draft London Plan was published 16 July 2026 and is not adopted policy
Draft-plan HRA identified pathways including recreation/urbanisation, air pollution and water resources and retained unresolved air-quality evidence for Epping Forest at publication
Current infrastructure guidance reiterates that HRA conclusions depend on project/site effects and the competent authority’s integrity test

examples: An EIA threshold or Schedule category does not prove that a specific candidate requires EIA until screening criteria and project details are applied
SEA/SA conclusions for a plan cannot be copied as project-level environmental clearance
HRA screening cannot be replaced by a simple distance buffer where impact pathways need assessment
A plan-level HRA does not automatically clear every later project
The Draft London Plan IIA is strategic evidence and not parcel due diligence
The 2026 HRA’s unresolved Epping Forest air-quality pathway demonstrates that uncertainty must remain explicit
A statutory-body consultation response requires sufficient proposal-specific information
No promotion without exact parcel/site relation plus the applicable project-level assessment gate
